open_points.subject: create-project replay after the created Project changes
open_points.text: “a retried create never makes a second project while the first keeps its values” does not define which Project facts count as “its values” or what a retry does after any of them changes
open_points.question: After a successful create, which later changes end its duplicate-prevention identity, and does a retry then return the existing Project, refuse, or create a new Project?
options: Only anonymisation or deletion ends recognition; corrections and archiving still return the existing Project
A change to any original create-supplied value ends recognition, so the retry creates a new Project
A changed or archived Project remains recognisable, but the retry is refused instead of returned
Any changed Project fact, including status, revision or last-changed instant, ends recognition
open_points.default_guess: Keep the request id authoritative until anonymisation or deletion and return the existing Project in its current state.

witness.initial: The owner has created active Project P with request id R, name N and object O; P retains R as State 1 requires.
events: The owner corrects P's display name from N to N2, moving its revision and last-changed instant.
The owner retries the original create request R with name N and object O after losing its original answer.
outcomes: Registry recognises R and returns the existing Project P, now carrying N2, without minting another identity.
Because P no longer keeps the create values, Registry treats the retry as a new create and mints Project Q in addition to P.
witness.observer: The owner sees either one or two projects in the catalogue, and downstream consumers can observe whether a second project identity exists.
